The Stop Line

The B Team can own this platform if it makes restraint visible through approved proof, named senior responsibility and clear limits before any artificial intelligence claim reaches the market.

It differentiates The B Team by refusing the broad artificial intelligence promise and showing the proof, owner and limit behind each claim.

It fits The B Team's strongest established proof: trusted software delivery, senior judgment and careful claims.

It can extend into proof pages, founder posts, partner packs, technical artifacts, sales material and talent content without changing the idea.

Competitors can talk about governance, but they cannot copy The B Team's approval route, named senior ownership and approved proof library unchanged.

It can travel across the United States, the European Union and Sofia because trust, proof and human responsibility are not local claims.

Signed by Humans

The B Team can own this platform if every serious artificial intelligence claim carries a visible human signature: who checked it, what proof supports it and where the system stops.

It stands apart because it makes human responsibility the proof point, not a decorative reassurance after an artificial intelligence claim.

It draws from The B Team's senior craft and approval discipline, which are already central to the strategy.

It can support founder visibility, technical credibility, recruitment, partner enablement and buyer follow-up because each use shows human ownership.

It creates a practical trust mechanism competitors cannot easily copy unless they expose their own approval route and senior accountability.

It is durable because buyers in different markets can understand a simple promise: a senior person still owns the work.

Paid supports targeted message testing, retargeting and amplification after proof exists; it drives buyers and partners to owned proof pages, then lifts earned stories and shared founder content rather than carrying the reputation story alone.

Earned leads this corporate reputation platform once the proof library and public identity cleanup are ready, because independent validation makes The Stop Line harder to dismiss and gives paid, shared and owned channels stronger proof to carry.

Shared makes senior ownership visible through founder, executive and team posts; it points audiences to owned proof, gives influencers and partners material they can repeat and helps paid amplification reach warmer audiences.

Owned is the proof base: website pages, proof library, approval language, case material, technical artifacts and sales follow-ups; paid drives to it, earned cites it and shared content turns it into a steady public signal.

Shared and Owned

The platform is The Stop Line, launched through Signed by Humans. Its purpose is to make The B Team's artificial intelligence story credible by showing approved proof, senior responsibility and the limit the system will not cross before any claim is promoted.

The rollout should move in this order: clean the public identity, lock the proof library, test the control-led owner message, launch the founder-led proof story and then seek earned validation. No delivery date is established beyond 30 June 2027.

The plan leads with owners of midsize businesses who want control and visibility, then equips technical buyers with proof. It also supports referral partners, ecosystem partners, enterprise buyers and senior Sofia talent with the same story, adapted to their role.

Owned runs always-on as the proof base: proof pages, approval language, case material, technical artifacts, sales follow-ups and frequently asked questions. Shared runs always-on through founder, executive and team posts. The newsroom watches for artificial intelligence trust, governance and buyer-risk moments, then responds only when The B Team has approved proof and a clear stop line to show. Earned leads reputation once proof exists, while paid supports testing, retargeting and amplification.

The main tactics are The Stop Line proof page, Signed by Humans founder launch post, partner proof pack, owner control message test and senior craft story series. Each tactic must trace to an audience, a key message and a communications pillar before it goes on the calendar.

The calendar should not be built as campaign bursts only. It should combine a few hero moments with steady hub content and hygiene updates, with the middle carrying most of the programme through proof pages, founder posts, buyer explainers, partner material and technical artifacts.

The sequence is proof before promotion. If a claim cannot show approved proof, a senior owner and the line the system will not cross, it does not ship; where approval or evidence is not established, the plan must say so instead of filling the gap.
